# Class factory API

RObjC uses four `RS*Class()` functions to declare R6-based classes and
protocols. Each returns a generator. Use `$new()` to instantiate object and
scalar classes; the singleton factories also create a shared instance during
declaration. A protocol generator describes requirements for classes.

| Factory | Declares | Shared instance |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `RSObjectClass()` | An ordinary object class | None |
| `RSProtocolClass()` | A protocol and its required method names | None |
| `RSSingletonClass()` | An object class with one prebuilt instance | `Class$instance` |
| `RSScalarClass()` | A scalar class and a generated NA subclass | `Class$na` |

## Common arguments and class identity

Object, singleton, and scalar factories accept `class_name`, `super_class`,
`protocols`, `public`, `private`, `active`, `parent_env`, and `version`.
`public`, `private`, and `active` supply R6 members; `protocols` is a list of
protocol generators. `RSProtocolClass()` instead takes `protocol_name`,
`super_protocols`, and `contract_methods`, plus `parent_env` and `version`.
The default `version` is `"1.0.0"`; a version must not contain `_`.
Normally, `parent_env` can be left at its default.

The factories attach `robjc_isa` metadata to the generator. Instances report
their generator through `$class()`. Class identity uses the generator rather
than only its name, so two separately declared classes with the same name are
not interchangeable. Use a non-singleton RObjC generator as `super_class`;
`RSScalarClass()` specifically requires `RSScalar` or a subclass.

## An ordinary object class

`RSObjectClass()` defaults to `RSObject` as its superclass. Declare methods in
`public` and create instances with `$new()`:

```{r}
library(robjc)

Widget <- RSObjectClass(
  "VignetteWidget",
  public = list(label = function() "widget")
)
widget <- Widget$new()
stopifnot(identical(widget$label(), "widget"))
stopifnot(identical(widget$class(), Widget))
```

## A protocol

`RSProtocolClass()` records required method names, not implementations.
`super_protocols` can inherit requirements from other protocols. Pass the
protocol generator in a class's `protocols` list, then implement its methods.
Protocol generators cannot create instances with `$new()`:

```{r}
Labeled <- RSProtocolClass(
  "VignetteLabeled",
  contract_methods = "label"
)
stopifnot(is.null(Labeled$new))
LabeledWidget <- RSObjectClass(
  "VignetteLabeledWidget",
  protocols = list(Labeled),
  public = list(label = function() "labeled widget")
)
stopifnot(LabeledWidget$new()$conformsTo(Labeled))
```

## A shared singleton

`RSSingletonClass()` calls `$new()` while declaring the class. Therefore its
initializer must work without arguments. The shared object is available as
both `Class$instance` and `Class$robjc_isa$slot`:

```{r}
Registry <- RSSingletonClass("VignetteRegistry")
stopifnot(identical(Registry$instance, Registry$robjc_isa$slot))
stopifnot(identical(Registry$instance$class(), Registry))
```

`$new()` remains callable; use `$instance` when the shared object is required.
`RSNull` is declared with `RSSingletonClass()` and exposes its shared object as
`RSNull$null`.

## A scalar class and its NA companion

`RSScalarClass()` requires a length-one missing `na_value` appropriate for the
new scalar type. It declares a regular class and an NA subclass, then creates
the NA subclass's shared instance. An `initialize(val)` method must accept
`na_value` during that construction and call `super$initialize(val)` first.
The regular class rejects direct construction with an NA; use `Class$na` for
missing values.

```{r}
Count <- RSScalarClass(
  "VignetteCount",
  na_value = NA_integer_,
  public = list(initialize = function(val) {
    super$initialize(val)
    if (!is.integer(val)) stop("Expected an integer scalar.")
    invisible(self)
  })
)
stopifnot(identical(Count$new(2L)$value(), 2L))
stopifnot(identical(Count$na$value(), NA_integer_))
stopifnot(identical(Count$na, Count$robjc_isa$slot))
stopifnot(identical(Count$na$class()$classname, "VignetteCountNA"))
```

Names starting with `RS` produce an `RSNA...` companion; other names receive
an `NA` suffix. The factory sets `isNAClass` before initializing the companion,
so type-specific initialization can distinguish it from regular instances.
By default, the generated NA class disables `$new()`; use `Class$na` for its
shared instance. With `na_singleton = FALSE`, the NA class remains directly
constructible so each missing value can retain its own metadata.
For choosing a constructor and distinguishing `NULL` from typed NA, see
`vignette("robjc_scalar_values", package = "robjc")`.
